title: Pointer telemetry bridge protocol
description: Wire contract shared by the input device, viewer/overlay clients and the Gemini bridge. Every JSON message is one UTF-8 text WebSocket frame carrying a discriminating `type` field; binary frames carry media (see $defs/mediaFrame). Coordinates are normalized to the unit square with (0,0) at the top-left of the input surface, so every client can rescale to its own viewport. The root schema is the union of all JSON frames in either direction; per-definition descriptions state their direction.

clientRole.description: input: emits telemetry and media. viewer: renders the shared pointer. gemini: relays Gemini Live function calls and results.

clientId.description: Stable identifier for a connection, chosen by the client or generated by the server.

unitFloat.description: Normalized coordinate in the unit square, (0,0) = top-left.

clientInfo.description: Roster entry describing one live WebSocket connection.

channelStats.description: State of one bounded media ring buffer. Oldest chunks are evicted once a byte or chunk limit is exceeded.

oldest_received_at_ms.description: Arrival time of the oldest buffered chunk, null when empty.

newest_received_at_ms.description: Arrival time of the newest buffered chunk, null when empty.

telemetry.description: input -> server. One pointer sample. Sent as often as the input device produces samples (typically on every move frame); the server re-broadcasts it as a telemetryEvent.

pinch_active.description: true while the pointer is pinching (finger down / drag engaged).

ts.description: Optional client capture timestamp; the server reports it back as client_ts.

seq.description: Optional client-side monotonic sample counter; reported back as client_seq.

telemetryEvent.description: server -> clients. A telemetry sample stamped and sequenced by the server, broadcast to every other connected client.

seq.description: Server-assigned broadcast sequence; strictly increasing across the process.

functionCall.description: Any direction. A call to one of the tools declared in x-gemini.tools, typically emitted by a Gemini Live session and relayed by the server. When `to` is present the server delivers it to that client only; otherwise it is broadcast to every other client.

call_id.description: Correlation id supplied by Gemini; echoed in the matching functionResult.

name.description: Tool name; must be one of the names declared in x-gemini.tools.

args.description: Tool arguments, validated by the tool's own parameters schema.

origin.description: Role that emitted the call; set by the server from the sender's role.

functionResult.description: Any direction. Outcome of a functionCall, correlated by call_id. The Gemini bridge forwards results back into the Live session as a function response.

result.description: Tool return value when ok is true.

error.description: Failure detail, required when ok is false.

stateSnapshot.description: server -> client, sent immediately after the WebSocket is accepted so a late joiner can paint the current pointer without waiting for the next sample.

telemetry.description: Most recent broadcast telemetry, null until the first sample arrives.

protocolError.description: server -> client. A frame was rejected. The connection stays open so a live input stream can recover without reconnecting.

code.description: One of invalid_json, invalid_payload, unknown_type, unknown_target, empty_frame, unsupported_channel, payload_too_large, busy.

detail.description: Optional structured context, e.g. failing field locations.

videoFrame.description: input -> server. One base64-encoded image as JSON, the JSON counterpart of a binary frame with tag 1. The server decodes data_base64 and appends the bytes to the video ring buffer, so consumers see one video stream regardless of transport. Use binary frames for high frame rates: base64 costs about 33% more bandwidth.

encoding.description: Image encoding of the decoded bytes.

data_base64.description: Standard base64 of exactly one encoded frame.

mediaFrame.description: NOT JSON: a binary WebSocket frame sent by an input client. Byte 0 is the channel tag (1 = video, 2 = audio) and bytes 1..n are one opaque, self-contained payload, e.g. a single JPEG or WebM cluster for video, or one PCM16/Opus chunk for audio. The server stamps the arrival time and appends the payload to that channel's bounded ring buffer; the encoding itself is negotiated out of band. A video frame may alternatively arrive as a videoFrame JSON message.

x-gemini.description: Function declarations for a Gemini Live API session. GET /api/gemini/tools serves this array verbatim as tools[0].function_declarations. set_pointer and set_pinch act on the shared pointer. log_instrument and verify_tray_count update the surgical tray log implemented in tools.py.

tools.name: set_pointer
tools.description: Move the shared pointer to a normalized position on the user's input surface. Use when the user asks to point at, touch or move to a location, for example 'point at the top right corner'.

x.description: Horizontal position: 0 is the left edge, 1 is the right edge.

y.description: Vertical position: 0 is the top edge, 1 is the bottom edge.

tools.name: set_pinch
tools.description: Press or release the shared pointer's pinch, starting or ending a drag or tap gesture without moving the pointer.

active.description: true to engage the pinch, false to release it.

tools.name: log_instrument
tools.description: Record a surgical instrument on the case log. Call this when the user adds an instrument to the tray, removes one, or notes that one was used. added and removed change the running tray count; used does not.

instrument.description: Common name of the instrument, for example scalpel, forceps, needle driver, or sponge.

action.description: added puts instruments on the tray, removed takes them off, and used records use without changing the on-tray count.

quantity.description: How many of that instrument this entry accounts for. Defaults to 1 when omitted.

notes.description: Optional detail such as size or laterality. Omit when the user gave none.

tools.name: verify_tray_count
tools.description: Compare the running tray count with the count the team expects. Call this when the user asks to verify, confirm, or reconcile the tray or one instrument. The actual count comes from earlier log_instrument calls. The result reports actual_count, matches, and delta (actual minus expected).

expected_count.description: How many the team expects to be on the tray right now.

instrument.description: Instrument to count. Omit, or leave empty, to verify the whole tray as one total.
